parsed.why: Sodomy statutes remain on the books but documented as unenforced; no trans-specific arrests, violence or border incidents. No recognition or anti-discrimination law and documented service discrimination, but no traveller-facing facility ban or state targeting: latent restriction plus thin recourse, not active exposure.

No criminalisation, but a national law bars restroom access by birth sex — a universal state-imposed exposure reaching every outed visitor — alongside repeal of anti-discrimination coverage and rising hate crime against trans women. Working recourse exists (torture conviction, court reversals), so Elevated, not lower.

Sodomy statute (one year, applies to women) enforced occasionally, with documented arrests of people after attackers invoked their identity, plus an active harsh-bill push. No trans-specific violence data and no traveller protections; employment clause is resident-facing. Worse than an unenforced paper statute.

No criminalisation, no border friction and no facility ban; hate-crime law covers orientation and institutions do prosecute. But a lethal targeted attack on a queer venue with condemned state inaction, hostile ministers and regressive bills push it below full acceptance tier.

Statute criminalises same-sex relations (10–15 years), gender-affirming care and diverse gender expression, with deportation among penalties; no recognition. Documented killings with impunity, the UN calling state neglect itself perpetration, and past militia sweeps against gender-nonconforming youth.
